query: For ultrasonic atomization of molten metals (sonotrode or vibrating-plate ultrasonic atomization, e.g. AMAZEMET rePowder, 3D Lab ATO Lab / ATO One, or lab-built 20-60 kHz systems), what published data exist on run-to-run or batch-to-batch repeatability at fixed process settings? Report, with numbers and citations: (a) the spread in particle size distribution (D10/D50/D90, span, or mass fraction in 15-45 um or 20-63 um) across replicate runs (standard deviation or coefficient of variation, and the number of replicates); (b) the spread in yield (fraction of the charge converted to powder, and fraction in the target size cut); (c) the spread in sphericity, circularity, aspect ratio or satellite fraction; (d) run-to-run variation in composition or oxygen pickup. Prioritize aluminum alloys (AlSi10Mg, Al-Si, 6xxx such as 6061/6063, Scalmalloy) but include other alloys (Ti, Fe, Ni, Cu, Mg, refractory). If true replicate data are absent, say so explicitly and give the closest proxies (error bars in parameter studies of amplitude, frequency or melt feed rate; repeated-measurement scatter), and list the process variables the literature identifies as the dominant sources of variability (amplitude, frequency, melt superheat, melt flow rate, sonotrode/plate material and temperature, wetting, oxygen).
